chains.title: ARID5B: ref T preserves a repressor site; alt C loses ARID5B and de-represses IRX3/IRX5
chains.element: dELS active distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3181208

links.claim: ARID5B binds the ref T allele more strongly than the alt C allele. ARID5B is not in QBiC-SELEX coverage (E37), so no QBiC-SELEX allelic effect is available for ARID5B; the literature search E35 specifically points to ARID5B/IRX3 enhancer allele-specific reporter work, but the supplied excerpts do not give the reporter result. The direction is therefore literature/motif-motivated, not proven by an assay in this evidence set.
The variant lies in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE (dELS), with DNase and H3K27ac signal consistent with a regulatory element.

IRX3 is a distal candidate target about 520 kb away; E17 reports alt C increasing IRX3 in pancreas (NES +0.37), and E35 points to an IRX3 enhancer model. This gene link is not adipose-specific and L2G favors FTO (E16), so it is indirect.

The disease-relevant context is subcutaneous adipose/preadipocytes; the element is active in the adipose context (E03) and the literature model is in preadipocytes (E35), but this evidence set does not provide ARID5B expression or ChIP occupancy in preadipocytes.

Loss of ARID5B binding on alt C is proposed to de-repress IRX3/IRX5, reduce thermogenic browning, and increase obesity risk. This predicts alt C as the risk allele; however, E15 labels T as the effect/risk allele, so the direction is discordant with the supplied GWAS label and must be resolved.

predictions: ARID5B ChIP-qPCR in preadipocytes will show higher ARID5B occupancy on ref T than alt C.
ARID5B knockdown in preadipocytes will increase IRX3/IRX5 expression.
An allele-specific reporter will show higher IRX3/IRX5 enhancer activity for alt C, abolished by ARID5B knockdown.
falsified_if: Allele-specific ARID5B ChIP in preadipocytes shows no ref-T preference at this base.
ARID5B knockdown or loss does not change IRX3/IRX5 in preadipocytes.
An allele-specific reporter in preadipocytes shows no C-allele effect on IRX3/IRX5 enhancer activity.

chains.title: ATF3: alt C increases binding at the FTO enhancer
chains.element: dELS active distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3181208

links.claim: ATF3 binds the alt C allele more strongly than ref T: QBiC-SELEX ATF3 own model gives z 21.73 and effect 1.403 (alt > ref). ATF3 is expressed in subcutaneous adipose (57.63 TPM, rank 88/1631), but its only ENCODE peak over this variant is in HCT116, not adipose, so adipose occupancy is not demonstrated.
The variant lies in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE (dELS) with DNase and H3K27ac signal, consistent with a regulatory element.

FTO is the best L2G gene at this locus (E16), but E36 reports no significant adipose eQTL for this variant, and the only FTO eQTL is in skeletal muscle with alt C giving NES +0.14 (E17). The gene link in the disease context is therefore weak.
ATF3 is expressed in subcutaneous adipose and the element is active there, but no adipose ATF3 ChIP is available; expression plus an active element does not demonstrate occupancy.

The locus is strongly associated with obesity/BMI (E15/E16). If ATF3 represses FTO in preadipocytes, stronger alt-C ATF3 binding would lower FTO and be protective relative to T; this is compatible with T being the E15 effect allele but is a specific prediction, not established by the data.

predictions: ATF3 ChIP-qPCR in preadipocytes will show higher occupancy on alt C than ref T.
ATF3 knockdown will change FTO expression in preadipocytes.
If ATF3 represses FTO, the alt C allele will lower FTO in adipose/preadipocytes.
falsified_if: Allele-specific ATF3 ChIP in preadipocytes shows no alt-C preference.
ATF3 perturbation does not change FTO in preadipocytes.
The alt-C allele does not alter FTO in adipose when ATF3 is manipulated.

chains.title: JUN: alt C increases AP-1 factor binding at the FTO enhancer
chains.element: dELS active distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3181208

links.claim: JUN binds the alt C allele more strongly than ref T: QBiC-SELEX JUN own model gives z 17.91 and effect 0.317 (alt > ref), with alt at the 99.8th percentile versus 82.8th for ref. JUN is very highly expressed in subcutaneous adipose (442.88 TPM, rank 3/1631), but its only ENCODE peak over this variant is in HepG2, not adipose.
The variant lies in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE (dELS); ENCODE ChIP-seq in other biosamples includes active-element factors such as EP300 and Pol II, consistent with an enhancer.

FTO is the best L2G gene at this locus, but E36 reports no significant adipose eQTL for this variant and the FTO eQTL is only in skeletal muscle (alt C NES +0.14, E17). The FTO gene link is plausible but not proven in adipose.
JUN is abundantly expressed in subcutaneous adipose and the element is active there, but no adipose JUN ChIP is available; expression does not demonstrate occupancy.

The locus is associated with obesity/BMI. JUN can activate or repress depending on context: if JUN activates FTO, alt C would increase FTO and make C risk, conflicting with E15's T effect allele; if JUN represses FTO, alt C would lower FTO and be protective, consistent with T as effect allele. The direction is unresolved.

predictions: JUN ChIP-qPCR in preadipocytes will show higher occupancy on alt C than ref T.
JUN perturbation will change FTO expression in preadipocytes.
The FTO direction will depend on whether JUN activates or represses FTO in adipocytes.
falsified_if: Allele-specific JUN ChIP in preadipocytes shows no alt-C preference.
JUN perturbation does not change FTO in preadipocytes.
The alt-C allele does not alter FTO in adipose when JUN is manipulated.
